models.title: Little Ruin Canyon & Square Tower Group — 1 m Airborne LiDAR Surface
models.classificationLabel: Observed survey · Airborne LiDAR (not a reconstruction)
models.scaleNote: 1:1 metric scale (UTM Zone 12N, meters; 749 m east-west × 519 m north-south; elevation 1,557.75–1,608.65 m NAVD88). Resampled from 1 m bare-earth DEM at 3 m grid spacing; hypsometric and slope shading applied for terrain legibility.

provenance.creator: U.S. Geological Survey — 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)
provenance.method: Airborne LiDAR 1-meter bare-earth Digital Elevation Model (tiles x66y414 and x67y414, EPSG:26912), cropped to Little Ruin Canyon head and triangulated into glTF 2.0 binary.
provenance.processing: Stitched tiles x66y414 (SHA-256 2ee10c4b…) and x67y414 (SHA-256 88c64ce8…), cropped to UTM 12N E 669,744–670,493 m / N 4,139,004–4,139,523 m, sampled at 3 m spacing, centered at local origin (0,0,0), with smooth normals and vertex elevation shading.

fallback.alt: Black-and-white HABS photograph of the north masonry walls and D-shaped tower of Hovenweep Castle perched on sandstone bedrock.
fallback.summary: Static HABS photograph shown initially so no 3D mesh bytes download until requested. Select Load interactive 3D model to inspect the 1 m USGS LiDAR topography of Little Ruin Canyon and its seven documented masonry complexes.
fallback.spatialNotes: Airborne bare-earth LiDAR resolves canyon rims, talus slopes, and drainage heads at 1–3 m scale; it does not resolve individual standing masonry wall courses, which are shown in the HABS measured drawings and photographs below.
